https://www.chvnradio.com/articles/waffl.text: Waffles, folk music, and tradition: A European journey at Folklorama The CHVN Cruiser started its evening at the Belgian Pavilion at Le Club Belge on Monday evening. There was a nice atmosphere of hospitality as pavilion staff and volunteers directed and assisted people throughout the evening. People could also experience Belgian cuisine with the famous Belgian waffle on the menu. Prior to the start of the show, trivia questions about Belgium were displayed for attendees to answer. During the show, Belgian history was shared including the origin of stilt dancing in Namur, Belgium. The show went on as dancers performed traditional dances to live music, and the audience got to participate in one of the dance routines. A post shared by CHVN 95.1 FM (@chvn951) RELATED STORIES: CHVN Cruiser explores three vibrant Folklorama pavilions on opening night Black History Manitoba celebrates Emancipation Day at Canadian Museum for Human Rights Folklorama's 55th festival celebrates Manitoba's diversity with citizenship ceremony Romanian Pavilion The Cruiser then dashed over to the Bronx Park Community Centre for the Romanian Pavilion. Festival-goers can take in the elaborate and detailed Cultural Display found in the foyer, that took hours of hard and dedicated work to create. "Every year we present a new theme that will showcase Romania and its wonders. It takes some time to do the research then to create posters and think about videos that we can display and support the information that we are bringing to the larger community in Winnipeg," shares Dori Bularca, Cultural Display Chairperson. A focal point of this year's display was highlighting the salt lakes of Romania. Bularca explains the theme of the year. "The main theme this year is 'Romania: Land of Healing and Rejuvenation'. I chose this theme because I do not believe many know in Romania, we have one third of all the hot springs of Europe. Sixty percent of all the mineral waters of all of Europe are in Romania." Traditional dances The evening was filled with traditional Romanian dances and featured Romanian traditional folk artist, Mircea Gheorgescu, who played a self-created pan flute musical instrument. The show took the audience through different seasons of the year and showcased different traditions and rites. "One of the beautiful things this year that is a bit different from previous years is that we're highlighting rituals and traditions, one per season," says Pavilion Emcee, Anna Stefanovici, B.A., M.Pub. The Romanian Pavilion is running until August 8 and tickets to the show can be purchased here . https://www.dw.com/en/ukraine-starlink-s.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5OdB5 Ukrainian soldiers handle a Starlink terminal Image: Dmytro Smolienko/Ukrinform/Avalon/Photoshot/picture alliance Advertisement The Starlink satellite system and its military version Starshield were fully functional on Saturday, the Ukrainian government said. Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy said speeds for Starlink and Starshield started returning to normal overnight. Ukraine's ‌defense ministry confirmed on Saturday that the connection remained stable at over 400 kilometers per hour (kph). "The main thing for today is ‌that Starlink and Starshield have resumed operations at their pre-restriction speeds. The speeds are now at the level we need," Zelenskyy said on Telegram. "This is crucial. This really matters: for our frontline logistics, for defending Ukraine against jet-powered 'Shaheds,'" he added. The announcement comes after over a week of Starlink and Starshield restrictions that disrupted military operations in Ukraine and sparked tensions with the US . Ukrainian officials said that the capped speeds of 160 kph had hampered the military's ability to intercept Russian attack drones and forced the cancellation of some operations. Did someone order Ukraine's high-speed Starlink shutdown? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video What caused Starlink's restrictions? Starlink is operated by rocket company SpaceX, owned by billionaire Elon Musk, who is a close ally of US President Donald Trump. US newspaper The Wall Street Journal (WSJ) reported earlier this week that US officials believed Musk acted unilaterally in capping the speeds at which Ukrainian hardware could stay connected to the satellite-based network. According to the WSJ report, officials signaled that Trump did not specifically order retribution against Kyiv. But in response to the report, Musk said that "any limits to speed or usage" of Starshied were "decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS." Both Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth have denied that the Pentagon had directed any changes. It remains unclear who is responsible for last week's Starlink slowdown. Kyiv has come to question Washington's support over intelligence sharing, amid speculation that the White House may have ordered the restrictions on Starshield. The Starlink slowdown came as the relationship between the US and Ukraine has become strained after President Donald Trump's reported deal with Moscow on Russian diesel imports , which Ukraine viewed as a betrayal.
